summary: Verified ASER pill inside Reports sub-menu for MOD user. Encountered a fatal ReferenceError (isMODacct is not defined) in /app/frontend/src/App.js line 873 that crashed the entire app post-login; fixed inline and confirmed all 4 ASER acceptance criteria pass.
action_items: Review the inline fix at App.js:873 (replaced undefined isMODacct with inline includes-check on user.account_type). Consider hoisting isMODacct to component scope for reuse.
Console shows /api KPI 403 errors on Reports/Performance KPIs for MOD users — non-blocking for ASER acceptance but worth investigating (endpoint auth/permissions for mod_site).
critical_code_review_comments: App.js line 208: isMODacct is scoped to AskPulseFitnessGuard but was referenced at line 873 in the main App component tree — caused Uncaught ReferenceError blocking ALL users. Introduced by commit 24e37b4e.
PulseReportsTab.js correctly gates the ASER sub-tab behind isMOD (mod_site/mod_branch/mod_org).
MODASERPortal renders with data-testid mod-aser-portal, dashboard cards (aser-dashboard-cards), and close (aser-close) — all wired correctly.
context_for_next_testing_agent: MOD ASER flow verified via UI: login modal -> Reports tab (lite-tab-reports) -> ASER sub-pill (pulse-report-sub-aser) -> overlay (mod-aser-portal) -> close (aser-close). No top-level lite-tab-aser exists. isMODacct scoping bug fixed inline in App.js.
rca_of_the_issue: Recent edit added `!isMODacct` guard on <FeedbackWidget /> inside the main App tree but did not declare isMODacct there; it only exists inside AskPulseFitnessGuard. Result: Uncaught ReferenceError on every render after user was set, showing runtime error overlay and preventing any further UI interaction. Fixed by inlining the includes check.
